longForm.overview:
⚠️ is the emoji of danger coded warning read — a clean warning-pulse shape, the danger filled-in silhouette, and the universal 'danger warning' tag for warning-marker. Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded warning read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded warning read, ⚠️ captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate danger coded warning — a 'danger ⚠️' warning-marker marker or a 'warning-pulse pulse ⚠️' warning-marker reveal. The danger fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern warning-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as danger coded rather than literal warning-coded shape.

In real-world usage ⚠️ lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate warning-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'danger ⚠️' warning-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'warning-pulse pulse ⚠️' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'danger coded ⚠️' list thread. The danger fill cue is what makes the emoji feel danger coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'danger coded warning moment.'

What separates ⚠️ from the rest of the shape family is the danger register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'danger coded warning,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why ⚠️ travels especially well on partner warning-marker markers, warning-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with danger energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip ⚠️ in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The danger coded warning cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid ⚠️ in 'literal object' or finish-coded contexts where the danger energy feels off. A 'danger ⚠️' message works for warning-marker marker; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip ⚠️ when you want to communicate a different color. The danger coded register is too danger-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
longForm.howToReply:

If the warning cue feels too danger coded, reply with a sharper emoji (◼ or ◻) that signals shape-coded energy without matching the danger volume.

When ⚠️ lands as a partner 'danger ⚠️' warning-marker marker, mirror with another ⚠️, a heart emoji, or a sentence that escalates the romance. When it arrives as a 'warning-pulse pulse ⚠️' list thread, mirror with another ⚠️, a sentence that joins the team energy, or a heart emoji that matches.
